 News › News News › Update Aadhaar biometrics if enrolled before age 15: NTA to JEE Main 2027 and other exam aspirants Update Aadhaar biometrics if enrolled before age 15: NTA to JEE Main 2027 and other exam aspirants
 Jasleen Taneja Updated: Nov 18, 2026, 14:00 IST Update Aadhar biometrics after age 15 The National Testing Agency (NTA) has shared an advisory for all candidates applying for NEET UG, JEE Main, CUET and other exams conducted by it to update the Aadhaar biometrics for hassle-free identity verification during the exam process.
 Candidates may face difficulties during biometric authentication at exam centres if their fingerprints or other biometric details do not match the records available with the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI).
 Candidates appearing for JEE Main, NEET UG, CUET and other NTA exams should check their Aadhaar details in advance and complete any pending biometric updates to avoid authentication-related problems during the exam process.
 Why update Aadhaar biometrics?
 Aadhaar-based authentication is used at different stages of the exam process, including registration through DigiLocker and identity verification at exam centres. NTA also uses biometric and facial authentication to verify candidate identities at exam centres.
 However, biometric details such as fingerprints and iris patterns can change as a person grows. As a result, the details captured when a candidate was a child may not match their current biometrics.
 This can create problems during identity verification, potentially delaying the entry process at exam centres. To avoid such issues, NTA has asked candidates to ensure that their Aadhaar biometric details are updated.
 According to the UIDAI guidelines, Aadhaar biometric details must be updated twice during childhood. The first update is required when a child turns five, while the second is required at the age of 15.
 The second update is particularly important for students preparing for entrance exams, as it replaces their childhood biometric records with updated details.
 Check the table below to know when biometric updates are required: 
 Aadhaar Stage Age Details Updated 
 Initial Enrolment 0 to 5 years Photograph; fingerprints and iris are not captured for children below five 
 First Mandatory Biometric Update (MBU) 5 years Fingerprints, iris and photograph 
 Second Mandatory Biometric Update (MBU) 15 years Fingerprints, iris and a fresh photograph 
 Candidates who completed their Aadhaar enrolment before turning 15 should check whether they have completed the second mandatory biometric update.
 Steps to update Aadhaar mandatory biometric
 Candidates can visit an authorised Aadhaar enrolment or update centre to complete the biometric update. The process involves the following steps:
 Visit the official UIDAI website, uidai.gov.in, to find the nearest Aadhaar enrolment or update centre. Candidates can book an appointment where the facility is available.
 Carry your Aadhaar card or Aadhaar number when visiting the centre.
 The centre will capture your fingerprints, iris details and a fresh photograph.
 After submitting the update request, collect the acknowledgement slip and note the Update Request Number (URN). Candidates can use this number to track the status of their request through the myAadhaar portal.
 Aadhaar Websites
 Candidates can visit the following official websites and helpline numbers for assistance:
 UIDAI Official Website: uidai.gov.in
 myAadhaar Portal: myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in
 UIDAI Helpline: 1947
 Checklist before applying for JEE Main 2027 and other NTA entrance exams
 Before filling out an application form for an NTA exam, candidates should check the following details:
 Their Aadhaar biometrics have been updated after turning 15.
 The biometric update request has been successfully processed and the status is reflected on the myAadhaar portal.
 The mobile number linked to Aadhaar is active to receive OTPs during online authentication.
 Their name and date of birth in Aadhaar match the details entered in the exam application form.
 Candidates should resolve any mismatch in their Aadhaar details before submitting their exam application to avoid last-minute difficulties.
